A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SegEarth-OV and provide readable main text, equations, seven tables, ten figures, and supplementary material. The shorter v2 appendix preserves all qualitative examples through a more compact layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original SegEarth-OV benchmark results, component ablations, and SimFeatUp evaluations in Tables 1–6, alongside qualitative comparisons and appendix data analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark, ablation, and qualitative results for SegEarth-OV and SimFeatUp, including the supplementary analyses and examples.

M1.justification: The SimFeatUp components, reconstruction losses, feature selection, shared JBU upsampling, attention modification, and global-token subtraction remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 17 remote-sensing datasets across four tasks, three natural-image evaluation datasets, and training data. The appendix dataset coverage and instance-size comparison are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout Tables 1–6, including the standard CLIP-based methods, remote-sensing backbones, and natural-image comparisons. The newly cited Cao et al. work is not added to an evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: Section 5.4 revises SkyCLIP's reported pretraining data size from 5.2M to 2.6M. This changes a stated training setting for an evaluated backbone; the ViT-B/32 evaluation procedure and Table 3 scores remain unchanged, and no experimental rerun is established.

E4.justification: The plug-and-play checks and component ablations in Tables 4–5, larger-image tests, backbone comparisons, and appendix instance-size analysis are retained. Consolidating Figures 8–10 does not remove qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Run and seed reporting and uncertainty practices are unchanged. Both versions retain point estimates without adding confidence intervals, repeated-run variability, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain their scores, including 39.2 average mIoU in Table 1 and 60.2 WBS-SI IoU in Table 2. Plotted and qualitative results also match. Changing 4% to 4.0% in the abstract is formatting only.

T1.justification: Equation (1) changes x to X to match the already defined input. This is a notation correction; the mathematical definitions, formulations, and reasoning otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same two proposed contributions, training-free framing, first-exploration claim, and performance claims across the four remote-sensing tasks.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 replaces a tentative explanation attributing GeoRSCLIP's advantage over SkyCLIP to more diverse images and descriptions with a broader inference that domain VLMs can benefit from diverse domain-specific data. Existing explanations of dataset difficulties and failure conditions remain.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 clarifies that OpenAI ViT-B/16 weights are the default, replacing the universal 'For all experiments' statement and aligning it with the existing ViT-B/32 study. Section 5.4 also revises SkyCLIP's pretraining-size documentation; hardware, hyperparameters, and resource-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Cao et al.'s Open-vocabulary remote sensing image semantic segmentation as contemporaneous training-required work. The DINO example and its reference are removed. This is a limited update to research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 corrects 'Traning-Free' in the title and elsewhere, expands the author and affiliation block, adds an SDG footnote, and makes localized wording, punctuation, and notation edits. The section organization is retained.

P2.justification: Figures 8–10 are reduced in size and consolidated from two appendix pages onto one, preserving all examples. Front matter and the Figure 5 caption receive small edits; table structures and other figure content remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity and positioning by acknowledging closely related contemporaneous work, reconciling the default-backbone description with the existing ViT-B/32 experiment, and correcting title and notation errors. The scientific evidence remains unchanged. Smaller appendix panels preserve the examples but reduce readability at normal page size, limiting the presentation benefit.
